key_insight: A PPO-based controller can coordinate battery, hydrogen, diesel, and grid exchange in a community microgrid to keep demand served with high renewable penetration under uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that reinforcement learning can improve operational resilience and economics for real-world hydrogen-enabled microgrids with coupled storage and variable renewable supply.
method: Formulated microgrid dispatch as an 11-state Markov decision process with three continuous actions.
Used proximal policy optimization (PPO) to control battery, diesel, and hydrogen dispatch.
Computed grid exchange from the residual power balance in a grid-connected community microgrid.
evidence_signal: Evaluated over 8,760 hourly observations for a 1,000-household community in Rockhampton, Australia, achieving A$195,690.67 annual revenue, 91.2% renewable fraction, 99.77% load satisfaction, and 0.085 kg CO2/kWh under the stated boundary.
watch_item: Performance depends on training stability, renewable profile variability, and the chosen accounting boundary, so deployment needs careful validation under local operating conditions.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy Management for Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids Under Uncertainty
